solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What could be mowed — a ——!

indicators.note: says the letters of the two words after it could be turned into something else entirely

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank riddle: name a thing that gets mown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges MOWED A, and the whole clue is also the definition, with the blank inviting the word that the letters make.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassy field of hay is the classic thing cut by a mower or scythe.

clue.text: Motorway dash that may make man mad

parts.note: the M1 motorway, written MI in crosswords
a sprint is a dash

explanation.surface: Rushing along the motorway may drive a person crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: a typo in 'man' can turn it into 'mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A typographical error swaps letters, so one could change one word into another.

clue.text: Actors somehow stifling vowels — terrible!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters smother the vowels by surrounding them
the letters are put together in some other way

parts.note: I, O and U are three vowels

explanation.surface: Actors muffling their vowels give a dreadful performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges ACTORS to ATROCS, which is 'stifling' IOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean appallingly bad or dreadful.

clue.text: Eight-day event in autumn month on avenue

indicators.note: in a down clue, the month sits on top of the avenue

parts.note: Oct is October

explanation.surface: An eight-day festival on an avenue in October.
explanation.walkthrough: In church use an octave is the eight days following a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: The church celebration spanning a feast day and the week after is eight days long.

clue.text: Scowls from operatic Peter grabbing Bill

indicators.note: the opera hero's name holds the bill's letters inside it

parts.note: Peter Grimes is the title character of Britten's opera
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: An opera singer playing Peter Grimes pulls faces on receiving a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Grimes is Benjamin Britten's opera about a Suffolk fisherman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are plural nouns for twisted facial expressions of displeasure.

clue.text: Food to go, ever put out where it ought be put out

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.words: where it ought be put out
parts.note: food is properly laid out on a table

explanation.surface: Takeaway food, always laid out where it belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' first rearranges TO GO EVER into ROOTVEGE, then its second sense, laid out, points to the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot or parsnip is an example of food grown underground.

clue.text: Country boy's old-fashioned curse

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A country lad swearing in an outdated way.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a malediction, the opposite of benison.

clue.text: Island included in their package travelling north

indicators.note: travelling north says the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters sit inside the two words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An island is part of the holiday deal, with travel heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Island included' as the definition, but 'included in' is the hiding signal; 'travelling north' reverses IRPAC up this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Meal is excellent, quietly eaten

indicators.note: the quiet letter is swallowed by the word for excellent

parts.note: super means excellent
p is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A meal is superb and consumed in silence.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening meal, usually a light one.

clue.text: Pole showing courage, one ousted

indicators.note: the letter standing for one is thrown out of the word for courage

parts.note: spirit is pluck or courage
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Pole displays bravery after one person is expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality; it is a spar on a sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprit is a small spar running diagonally to extend a sail, a kind of pole.

clue.text: Last word from pilot, dope flying all over the place

indicators.note: the letters of the two words scatter wildly, as an erratic aircraft would

explanation.surface: A doped-up pilot's final message as his plane careers about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying all over the place' rearranges PILOT DOPE; the airman flavour suits the old RAF-style farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated British goodbye, so it is what one says on leaving, a parting phrase.

clue.text: Involved in blunder, ye act heartlessly and refuse to acknowledge what's wrong

indicators.note: the letters are tangled together into a new order
the middle letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: Implicated in a mistake, you behave callously and ignore wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes C out of ACT to leave AT; 'Involved' rearranges IN BLUNDER YE AT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for deliberately ignoring misconduct, from Nelson raising his telescope to his blind eye.

clue.text: Get back with dog, having crossed St Paul's area?

indicators.note: the dog's name straddles the postcode, which sits inside it

parts.note: Rover is a stock name for a dog
St Paul's Cathedral is in the EC (East Central) postal district of London

explanation.surface: Retrieving something after a dog has wandered across the cathedral precinct.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the City of London postcode area that includes St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain or retrieve something lost is a synonym of the verb phrase.

clue.text: From harvest I get a small amount

indicators.note: the letters are drawn out of the run of three words that follow

explanation.surface: A farmer's complaint that the harvest yields very little.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace or tiny remnant of something is a little bit of it.

clue.text: Time for numbers to face each other

parts.note: NO is the standard short form of number, and the plural asks for two of them

indicators.note: the second copy is turned round so the pair look at one another

explanation.surface: A cue for performers to turn and face one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numbers' is plural, so the abbreviation appears twice, and the facing pair make a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a particular time of day, twelve o'clock.

clue.text: Changing some, but not all, decorations

indicators.note: only part of the two words is used, dropping their outer letters

explanation.surface: Swapping a few of the room's ornaments rather than the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains and tapestries hung on walls serve as decorations.

clue.text: Group of oppressed workers foaming at the mouth?

explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words it is a gang of slaves; read as one it means dribbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrase it is a gang of slaves; as one word it means drooling saliva.

clue.text: A road beset by various green bits? Maybe I've planted things

indicators.note: the article and road are surrounded by the jumbled letters
the letters of the colour word are arranged in a different way
the colour word is broken into bits and reassembled

explanation.surface: A road lined with assorted greenery, as though someone had planted it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bits' sits loosely beside 'various' as the scrambling signal; 'beset by' means the jumbled colour surrounds the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts in plants would say they had done so, so the 'I' is a typical horticulturist.

clue.text: One Greek character in bluish- grey is mimic

indicators.note: the first two pieces go inside the colour word

parts.note: slate is a bluish-grey colour
I is the Roman numeral one
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A single Greek actor dressed in grey is a copycat.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate or fake something is a verb synonym of copy.

clue.text: Barren spot — it takes time to establish a firm connection

indicators.note: the barren spot takes the time after it

parts.note: a moor is open barren upland
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Taming a barren patch of land is a long job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to establish' is a link here; the definition is a boat's secure tie-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring for a vessel holds it fast, so it is a secure attachment.

clue.text: Father of art movement

definitions.meaning: the early 20th-century anti-art movement of Duchamp and others

explanation.walkthrough: The same word is a nursery name for a dad and the name of an avant-garde art movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby-talk word for a parent, and the name of the Dadaist movement in art.

clue.text: Concert starts with piano trio on time

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A concert opens with a piano trio performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Punctual, happening at the right moment.

clue.text: I, wise man, said the ground would be frozen now

definitions.text: the ground would be frozen now

indicators.note: the pieces are spoken out loud, as in speech

parts.note: I plus a sage, a wise man

explanation.surface: A sage predicting that the ground will freeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns I SAGE into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacial period describes a time when frost and ice cover the land.

clue.text: Asian city managed to endure

parts.note: ran means managed, as one runs a business
go on means continue or last

explanation.surface: An Asian city organised to last.
explanation.definitionFit: The former name of Yangon, the largest city of Myanmar.

clue.text: Darkness is near, light's ending

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Dark approaches as the light fades.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours between dusk and dawn.

clue.text: Footballer getting goal in the last few minutes?

parts.note: a back is a defender in football
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A defender scoring late in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing part of a period or event, such as the final stage of a game.

clue.text: College dean, male drunk outside back of building

indicators.note: the scrambled letters wrap round the other piece
a drunk person's words are jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
takes the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A tipsy male college dean outside the rear of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges DEAN MALE, which goes 'outside' G, the 'back of' building.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalene is a Cambridge college, as Magdalen is in Oxford.

clue.text: One's charged — before long one's imprisoned

indicators.note: the letter for one is locked inside the word for soon

parts.note: anon means soon
I is one, and the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: An accused person learns they will soon be jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's charged' reads like a court case; it means something carrying an electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A negatively charged ion is a particle bearing an electrical charge.

clue.text: Heartless type, the leftie must be restricted

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word are taken away

parts.note: a red is a left-winger

explanation.surface: A cruel left-winger needs to be kept in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes YP from TYPE to leave TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied up with a rope or chain, and so confined in movement.

clue.text: Man, one ordained, set about lay worker

indicators.note: the two pieces are turned round to read the other way

parts.note: Reg is a man's name
Rev is short for a reverend, an ordained minister

explanation.surface: A man and a priest set upon a church layman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' turns REGREV round.
explanation.definitionFit: A church caretaker and attendant who is not ordained, so a lay official.
